caption: why is he collecting villagers 🛶
logline: A villager kid is dragged out of her village in a boat by a man who calls her number forty and already took her Mom and her uncle, who never came back; she thinks it's the best trip ever, and at dusk the boat bumps into the empty village across the water, every window lit, Mom and her uncle at the dock beside the old librarian who'd been alone for years.
question: why tf is this man dragging a villager kid across the grass in a boat?
premise: A man (a player) pulls a baby villager out of Oakend in an oak boat on a lead, across the grass. He calls her number forty. He took her Mom last week and her uncle before that, and none of them came back. Before they left he looked across the water at the old empty village, where only one window is lit, and said someone's been alone a long time. She thinks this is the best trip ever.
twist: Every Minecraft player knows a villager dragged in a boat is going to a trading hall. He isn't building one. He is filling Fernbank, the empty village across the inlet where the old librarian has lived alone with the golem for years, one villager at a time: number forty is the fortieth neighbour he has brought her. At dusk the boat bumps the dock, every window is lit, and Mom and the uncle are waiting at the dock's foot beside the librarian. 'None of them came back. They must love it there' was true.
mood_note: the score reads as a fun trip with an uneasy undertone for a player (tense, light), then warm on the reveal; if 'tense' plays too dark under a bubbly kid, 'funny' then 'heroic'
payoff_note: the picture lands on EMPTY (the cut to the lit village); S11 opens about 0.6 s after L10 ends and holds 1.6 s (the cold reader: 1 s is too short to pick out Mom, Uncle and the librarian) on Mom, Uncle and the librarian; the Short ends there. No line after L10.

world.canon: New: the man (a player, nameless) has been bringing villagers to Fernbank one at a time for a while before day 6000, from Oakend and elsewhere; the kid is the fortieth. From day 6000 Fernbank is a living village again: every house lit, about 40 villagers, the librarian no longer alone; the golem still by the well; the empty boat still at the dock; the HELLOBUH graves unchanged. Oakend loses the kid's family (her Mom, her uncle, her). Bible: World.

[A kind man in his thirties, low and warm, full voice]

lines.text: A MAN / pulled me out / of my VILLAGE / in a BOAT. / Across the GRASS.
lines.say: A man pulled me out of my village in a boat. Across the grass.
lines.direction: delighted, one quick breath, telling a friend the best news; the last word lands

lines.text: He calls me / number FORTY. / He's GOOD / at COUNTING.
lines.say: He calls me number forty. He's good at counting.
lines.note: 0a: 'number forty' misread as a skill (he is counting the villagers he has carried home, not stock for a hall)

lines.direction: pure joy, bouncing with the boat
lines.note: 0a: the kid thinks a boat dragged over grass is a fun ride (players know it is how villagers are moved to trading halls)

lines.text: Before we LEFT, / he looked across the WATER / at the old / EMPTY village. / Only ONE window / was LIT.
lines.say: Before we left, he looked across the water at the old empty village. Only one window was lit.
lines.direction: storytelling, a little hushed wonder but full voice, quick
lines.note: must-change 1: the lonely one is planted AT Fernbank, the village the boat will reach (one lit window: the librarian's)

lines.text: Someone's been ALONE / a long TIME.
lines.say: Someone's been alone a long time.
lines.direction: kind and low, looking across the water, not sad-dramatic
lines.note: the man's one line (must-change 1), on screen while he says it

lines.text: I think / he means HIMSELF. / He doesn't have / any FRIENDS.
lines.say: I think he means himself. He doesn't have any friends.
lines.direction: sure of it, sweet, a little sorry for him
lines.note: 0a: the kid's innocent misreading of 'someone' (it is the old librarian across the water)

lines.text: He took MOM / last WEEK. / And my UNCLE / before THAT.
lines.say: He took Mom last week. And my uncle before that.
lines.direction: bright, a fun fact, no worry at all
lines.note: the turn: for a player this is the dark beat (a man taking a family one by one); S07 on MOM, S07b on UNCLE

lines.text: None of them / came BACK. / They must / LOVE it there.
lines.say: None of them came back. They must love it there.
lines.direction: cheerful and certain, a shrug in the voice
lines.note: 0a: the kid reads 'never came back' as 'they love it' (a player reads trading-hall cells); literally true after the reveal

lines.text: At the WATER, / he SWAM / and pulled me BEHIND him. / The boat finally / got to SWIM!
lines.say: At the water, he swam and pulled me behind him. The boat finally got to swim!
lines.direction: giggling, the best part of the trip
lines.note: vanilla: a leashed boat follows its holder on water too (a lead does nothing only while a player sits in the boat); the villager can't leave the boat on its own

lines.text: When it got DARK, / we bumped into / the old / EMPTY village.
lines.say: When it got dark, we bumped into the old empty village.
lines.direction: a little slower, curious, still happy; the last word a small wonder
lines.note: the reveal starts on EMPTY: the cut to S10 lands on it (every window of the 'empty' village lit, villagers at their doors). The kid says nothing about what the picture shows; S11 follows with no line
